text: Introduction Perhaps every generation believes that it has reached a turning point of history, but our problems seem particularly intractable and our future increasingly uncertain.

Introduction 
Perhaps every generation believes that it has reached a turning point of 
history, but our problems seem particularly intractable and our future 
increasingly uncertain.

text: Many of our difficulties mask a deeper spiritual crisis.
text_raw:
Many of our difficulties mask a deeper spiritual 
crisis.

text: During the twentieth century, we saw the eruption of violence on an unprecedented scale.

on an unprecedented scale.

another has kept pace with our extraordinary economic and scientific 
progress.

text: We seem to lack the wisdom to hold our aggression in check and keep it within safe and appropriate bounds.
text_raw:
We seem to lack the wisdom to hold our aggression in check and 
keep it within safe and appropriate bounds.

text: The explosion of the first atomic bombs over Hiroshima and Nagasaki laid bare the nihilistic self­ destruction at the heart of the brilliant achievements of our modern cul­ ture.

atomic bombs over Hiroshima and Nagasaki laid bare the nihilistic self­
destruction at the heart of the brilliant achievements of our modern cul­

text: We risk environmental catastrophe because we no longer see the earth as holy but regard it simply as a "resource." Unless there is some kind of spiritual revolution that can keep abreast of our technological genius, it is unlikely that we will save our planet.
